subtitle: M4 · Game Boy Color

body: Resident Evil Gaiden is M4's Game Boy Color adventure about Barry Burton searching for Leon Kennedy aboard a passenger ship struck by a viral outbreak. Corridors and rooms are explored from above, with weapons, keys and supplies supporting the search through the vessel. The smaller screen gives the ship a different form from the series' fixed-camera console spaces. An approaching zombie still creates an immediate problem, but entering combat changes the display and asks the player to handle the threat through timing rather than ordinary movement around the room.

Combat switches to a first-person arrangement with a marker moving across a horizontal bar. Pressing the action button when it aligns with the enemy determines the attack's result. The encounter separates aiming from the exploration controls, turning each shot into a brief timing challenge. Ammunition and healing items remain useful discoveries aboard the ship. The player moves between carefully checking the map and reacting to the next creature, with the cost of a failed attempt carrying back into the resources available for the continuing search.

Barry and Leon encounter Lucia, a girl with an unusual connection to the weapon being carried aboard the Starlight. Their investigation gives the changing decks and corridors a continuing mystery beyond the immediate outbreak. Published first in Europe in 2001, Gaiden takes the series' characters and equipment into a substantially different structure. Its uneven reception reflected that change, but it remains a distinctive adaptation of survival horror to the handheld: exploration preserves the careful management of supplies, while fighting compresses the dangerous instant of a shot into a readable moving target.
story_headings: Stop the marker over the target
A different portable interpretation of the series
